description: Figure 5(b) is a line plot that compares the performance of various models during training from scratch by plotting the ratio of their loss to the loss of the Vanilla model against the number of FLOPs (floating-point operations). The x-axis, labeled "FLOPs," is a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^4$ to $10^7$. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Ratio w.r.t FLOPs," is a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4. The plot contains six distinct lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla (purple, dashed), StrmLLM(n=64) (blue, solid), SepLLM(n=64) (orange, dashed), SepLLM(n=64, H) (green, dotted), SepLLM(n=64, H/T) (red, dash-dotted), and SepLLM(n=128) (black, dash-dotted). All lines show a general downward trend, indicating that the loss ratio decreases as the number of FLOPs increases. The Vanilla model starts at a loss ratio of 3.4 and decreases to approximately 2.5. The StrmLLM(n=64) model starts at a ratio of about 3.2 and decreases to around 2.6. The SepLLM(n=64) model starts at a ratio of approximately 3.1 and decreases to about 2.7. The SepLLM(n=64, H) model starts at a ratio of about 3.0 and decreases to around 2.8. The SepLLM(n=64, H/T) model starts at a ratio of approximately 3.1 and decreases to about 2.7. The SepLLM(n=128) model starts at a ratio of about 3.2 and decreases to around 2.6.
